subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic core plugin circuit breaker, and what permanent plugin-runtime API, fail modes, persistence model, and default rollout should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fix changes core plugin semantics, persisted runtime state, operator controls, and compatibility defaults, which automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core breaker first
options.body: Open a maintainer design pass for a generic plugin-runtime breaker, then implement the agreed API/storage/defaults behind a staged rollout.

options.title: Keep breaker ownership plugin-local
options.body: Leave the broad framework issue open only as a policy discussion and continue adding targeted plugin-owned breakers where each owner can define degradation behavior.

options.title: Defer active degradation
options.body: Ship only hook timing, attribution, and status telemetry now, with active open/half-open behavior postponed until thresholds and fail modes are proven.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker first
recommendation.body: Open a maintainer design pass for a generic plugin-runtime breaker, then implement the agreed API/storage/defaults behind a staged rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin hook and registry work makes this the closest code-history owner for the core runtime API choice.
